target.title: Add per-tenant rate limiting to the API gateway

summary: Synthetic showcase. A token bucket per tenant now guards every /api route. Start with the bucket's refill math, then the middleware that owns the bucket map. The map is never pruned, and Retry-After is a fixed 1 second.

files.summary: New token bucket. Refill is lazy: each take() first credits tokens for the time since the last call, capped at capacity. Tokens are fractional, so a tenant at 1 token per second regains a whole token only after a full second.
files.pseudocode:
take(cost):
  tokens = min(capacity, tokens + elapsed_ms * refill_per_ms)
  if tokens < cost: reject
  tokens -= cost; allow

trace.before: No limiter. All four calls reach the router.
trace.after:
t=0 allow (1 left)
t=10 allow (0.01 left)
t=20 reject (0.02 < 1)
t=1020 allow (1.02 → 0.02)

callouts.text: now() defaults to Date.now, which can move backwards after an NTP correction. A negative elapsed time removes tokens. performance.now() is monotonic.
retryAfterSeconds ignores its argument and always returns 1. The middleware hard-codes the same value instead of calling it.

files.summary: The middleware creates one bucket per tenant on first sight and rejects with 429 when take() fails. The tenant header is client-supplied, so any caller can mint unlimited buckets.

callouts.text: buckets is a Map keyed by an untrusted header and never evicted. A client that rotates x-tenant-id grows it without bound.

files.summary: Default limit of 60 requests with 1 per second refill, plus one internal override.
Mounts the gateway in front of the API router only. Health checks outside /api are not limited.
